evidence_items.publisher: arXiv; Brohan and colleagues, Google DeepMind
evidence_items.explanation: The July 2023 evaluation explicitly treats a transformer-based robotics policy as state of the art. That is material transformer use in a named area, although it does not establish dominance across all robotics.

evidence_items.locator: Section 5, Model distillation; architecture also described in Section 1
evidence_items.explanation: DINOv2 uses vision transformers as its core visual backbones and reports leading general-purpose feature performance across image and pixel benchmarks. Transformers were therefore central to an important contemporary image-interpretation system.

evidence_items.publisher: International Planning Competition; Drexler and colleagues
evidence_items.locator: Post-Competition Analysis; component architectures described under Planners
evidence_items.explanation: The winning submitted planner combines classical search systems rather than a transformer architecture, supporting the planning example. The availability date refers to the public competition result; the current abstract also includes subsequent analysis.
The official results identify Ragnarok as the optimal-track winner and date the public announcement. This anchors the planner result before the post.

unresolved_gaps: The evidence does not provide a census of transformer use across all named areas.
Game playing, scientific applications and the many forms of reasoning are not comprehensively assessed.
The exact posting date of the current, expanded Ragnarok abstract is not established; its competition result and submitted system predate the post.
